title: Multiplication formula for Hernandez and Leclerc's quivers with potentials

candidates.error_location: Definition 2.2 and the sentence after it (identification of M[a,b] with a shifted module K^{(i)}_k)
candidates.exact_quote: M[a, b] is equal to the image of the \( q^{p_a} K^{(i_a)}_{\frac{p_a-p_b}{2}} \) under the map \(\Phi\)
candidates.claim_content: Setting: for an admissible sequence c = (i_k,p_k)_{k in Z} one has the condition p_{s^+} = p_s + 2, where s^+ = min{t | t > s, i_t = i_s}; hence for an i-box [a,b] (a ≤ b, i_a = i_b) one has p_b = p_a + 2m with m ≥ 0, i.e. p_b ≥ p_a. The paper defines M[a,b] by the exact sequence 0 → M[a,b] → I_{(i_a,p_a)} → I_{(i_b,p_b)} → 0 (generic kernel) and then asserts that M[a,b] = Φ( q^{p_a} K^{(i_a)}_{(p_a-p_b)/2} ), where K^{(i)}_k (k ∈ Z_{>0}) is the graded module over the generalized preprojective algebra defined by 0 → K_k^{(i)} → q^{k d_i} I_i(∞) →^{ε_i^k} q^{-k d_i} I_i(∞) → 0, and Φ : Π̃-gmod ≅ A-mod is the grading-to-vertex isomorphism, which satisfies Φ(q^{r-k d_i} K_k^{(i)}) = K_{k,r}^{(i)}.
candidates.suspected_defect: With p_b ≥ p_a, the index (p_a - p_b)/2 of K is ≤ 0, so K^{(i_a)}_{(p_a-p_b)/2} is not defined (K_k is defined only for k > 0); the index should presumably be (p_b-p_a)/(2 d_i). Moreover the grading shift is inconsistent with the paper's own rule Φ(q^{r-k d_i}K_k)=K_{k,r}: shifting (4.5) so that the middle term is q^{p_a} I gives submodule q^{p_a - k d_i} K_k, not q^{p_a} K_k. Also d_i is missing from the index (should be divided by 2d_i, not 2).

candidates.error_location: Short exact sequence displayed right after Definition 2.2
candidates.claim_content: The paper claims the exact sequence 0 → Φ^{-1}(M[a,b]) → q^{p_a} I_{i_a} →^{ε_i^{(p_a-p_b)/2}} q^{p_b} I_{i_a} → 0, where ε_i is the loop at vertex i of the generalized preprojective algebra Π̃ with bidegree deg(ε_i) = (b_ii, 0) = (2 d_i, 0), and I_i(∞) denotes the graded injective. The basic exact sequence is 0 → K_k^{(i)} → q^{k d_i} I_i(∞) →^{ε_i^k} q^{-k d_i} I_i(∞) → 0, i.e. multiplication by ε_i^k lowers the grading shift by 2k d_i. For the i-box [a,b], the admissibility condition p_{s^+}=p_s+2 forces p_b ≥ p_a.
candidates.suspected_defect: The exponent of ε in the map is written (p_a - p_b)/2, which is ≤ 0 since p_b ≥ p_a, and in the symmetrizable case should be (p_a-p_b)/(2 d_i) rather than (p_a-p_b)/2. Either the direction of the map (p_a vs p_b) or the sign/normalization of the exponent is wrong; the stated sequence is inconsistent with (4.5) and with the definition of K^{(i)}_{k,m} as kernel of I_{i,m} → I_{i,m-k b_ii}.

candidates.exact_quote: The module \( M^{-\infty} := \bigoplus_{a \in \mathbb{Z}_{<0}} M[a,0] \) is a rigid module, and the Gabriel quiver \( Q^{-\infty} \) of the endomorphism ring \( \text{End}_A(M^{-\infty}) \) equals \( Q_{GLS} \).
candidates.claim_content: In the paper, Q_{GLS}(c) is a quiver with vertex set Z (arrows: s → t if s^- < t^- < s < t and i_s ∼ i_t, and s → s^-), and its subquiver Q^-_{GLS}(c), the inverse image of Γ^-, has vertex set Z_{≤0} (the cluster algebra A has initial seed ((z_k)_{k ∈ Z_{≤0}}, Q_{GLS}(c), Z_{≤0})). Theorem 2.3 claims that M^{-∞} := ⊕_{a ∈ Z_{<0}} M[a,0] is rigid over A and that the Gabriel quiver of End_A(M^{-∞}) equals Q_{GLS}.
candidates.suspected_defect: Vertex-count mismatch: the direct sum runs over a ∈ Z_{<0}, so End_A(M^{-∞}) has one indecomposable summand for each strictly negative index, while the relevant quiver Q^-_{GLS}(c) has vertex set Z_{≤0} (including 0). Also the claimed equality is with Q_{GLS} (vertex set Z), not Q^-_{GLS}. Hence the Gabriel quiver of End_A(M^{-∞}) cannot literally equal Q_{GLS} (or Q^-_{GLS}) as stated — an index range error.

candidates.exact_quote:
Using isomorphism (2.4), we derive
\[
\operatorname{Ext}^1_A(M_1, M_2) \cong D\operatorname{Ext}^1_A(M_2, M_1) \tag{3.2}
\]
candidates.claim_content: Proposition 2.1 of the paper states: if M and N are modules over the generalized preprojective algebra Π̃ which are locally free over Π(l) = Π̃/ε^l Π̃ for some l, then Ext^1_A(Φ(M),Φ(N)) ≅ D Ext^1_A(Φ(N),Φ(M)), where Φ : Π̃-gmod ≅ A-mod is an isomorphism of categories and A = CΓ^-/J is the Jacobian algebra of Hernandez–Leclerc's quiver with potential. In Section 3.2 the paper asserts (3.2) Ext^1_A(M_1,M_2) ≅ D Ext^1_A(M_2,M_1) for arbitrary finite-dimensional A-modules M_1, M_2, with no local-freeness hypothesis, and uses this in the proof of Theorem 3.2 (e.g. to identify χ(P Ext^1_A(M_1,M_2)) with χ(P Ext^1_A(M_2,M_1))).
candidates.suspected_defect: The symmetry of Ext^1 is asserted for arbitrary A-modules, while the only justification given (Proposition 2.1 via GLS17 Thm 1.8) requires the modules to be locally free over some Π(l). A Jacobian algebra of this kind need not satisfy 2-Calabi–Yau-type Ext^1 duality for non-locally-free modules, so (3.2) is stated more generally than the argument supports, and Theorem 3.2 depends on it.

candidates.exact_quote:
Let \( M \) and \( N \) be two modules over \( \widetilde{\Pi} \), locally free over \( \Pi(l) \) for some \( l \), then we have:
\[
\operatorname{Ext}_A^1(\Phi(M), \Phi(N)) = D \operatorname{Ext}_A^1(\Phi(N), \Phi(M)) \tag{2.5}
\]
candidates.claim_content: Π̃ is the generalized preprojective algebra defined as the quotient of the path algebra of the quiver Q̃ (vertices I, arrows α_{ij} for i ∼ j and loops ε_i) by the relations ε_i^{-c_{ij}} α_{ij} = α_{ij} ε_j^{-c_{ji}} and Σ_{j∼i} Σ_{k=0}^{-c_{ij}-1} ω_{ij} ε_i^k α_{ij} α_{ji} ε_i^{-c_{ij}-1-k} = 0. Setting ε = Σ_i ε_i^{r/d} e_i, the algebra Π(l) := Π̃/ε^l Π̃. The claimed statement: for M, N modules over Π̃ that are locally free over Π(l) for some l, Ext^1_A(Φ(M),Φ(N)) ≅ D Ext^1_A(Φ(N),Φ(M)). The proof invokes [GLS17, Theorem 1.8], which gives Ext^1_Π(M,N) ≅ D Ext^1_Π(N,M) for locally free modules over the (finite-dimensional) generalized preprojective algebra Π of GLS.
candidates.suspected_defect: GLS17's Ext^1-duality is stated for locally free modules over GLS's preprojective algebra Π (essentially Π(1)), not for modules over Π̃ or over Π(l) with l > 1; moreover Ext groups computed over Π(l) need not agree with Ext over Π̃ (or over A). The cited theorem therefore does not obviously cover the stated hypotheses, so the proof of (2.5) is a gap.

candidates.claim_content: Setting: η : 0 → M_2 → m(η) → M_1 → 0 is an extension of A-modules; a splitting V = W ⊕ T of the underlying vector space is chosen with dim W = dim M_2 (so W carries M_2 and T carries M_1), and m(η) is given by matrices x_h = [[x_{2,h}, u_h],[0, x_{1,h}]] for each arrow h. For a pair (T', W') with T' ⊂ T a subrepresentation of M_1 and W' ⊂ W a subrepresentation of M_2, elements z ∈ Hom_I(T', W/W') (I-graded linear maps) give V_z = (W',0) + {(z(t),t) | t ∈ T'}, and V_z is a submodule iff x_{2,h} z(t) - z x_{1,h}(t) + u_h(t) ∈ W' for all t ∈ T'. The paper concludes that for two such z_1, z_2 the difference satisfies (x_{2,h}(z_1-z_2) - (z_1-z_2)x_{1,h})(T') ⊂ W', hence z_1 - z_2 ∈ Hom_A(M_2, M_1|_{W/W'}) and q_η^{-1}(T',W') ≅ Hom_A(M_2, M_1|_{W/W'}).

The displayed identification of the fiber is therefore with the wrong Hom-space (though it is still an affine space, so the Euler-characteristic conclusion survives).

candidates.suspected_defect: Two gaps: (i) additivity of g-vectors / injective presentations does not by itself produce a short exact sequence between M_1, T, M_2 (the presentations only match in K-theory); (ii) even granting such a sequence, rigidity of T does not immediately identify T with the generic extension M_1 * M_2 (one needs that the extension variety has a dense orbit and that the rigid module lies in it). Both steps are asserted as 'easy to see'.

candidates.exact_quote: Following the above Lemma and [KKOP24, Theorem 7.20], \( M^{-\infty} \) is a tilting module over \( A \). We will calculate the Gabriel quiver of \( \operatorname{End}_A(M^{-\infty}) \). It is directly deduced from [BIRS09, Theorem II.4.1]
candidates.claim_content: Theorem 2.3 claims M^{-∞} = ⊕_{a ∈ Z_{<0}} M[a,0] is rigid over A = CΓ^-/J (the Jacobian algebra of Hernandez–Leclerc's quiver Γ^- with potential S) and that the Gabriel quiver of End_A(M^{-∞}) equals Q_{GLS}. The proof deduces first that M^{-∞} is a tilting module (from Lemma 4.4, which only gives Ext^1_A(M[a_1,b_1],M[a_2,b_2]) = 0 for commuting i-boxes), and then computes the Gabriel quiver via [BIRS09, Theorem II.4.1], a result about cluster-tilting objects in 2-Calabi–Yau triangulated categories / stably 2-CY Frobenius categories.
candidates.suspected_defect: (i) Ext^1-vanishing among the summands gives rigidity, not tilting (projective dimension/resolution conditions are not checked); (ii) [BIRS09, Thm II.4.1] is stated for 2-Calabi–Yau categories, whereas A-mod is the module category of a Jacobian algebra which the paper itself says is not known to be the endomorphism ring of a tilting object over a preprojective algebra (Conjecture 2.4). Invoking it 'directly' applies a lemma outside the conditions under which it was stated.

candidates.claim_content: In the quiver Γ (with vertex set a connected component of I × Z) arrows are defined by: ((i,r) → (j,s)) ⟺ (b_{ij} ≠ 0 and s = r + b_{ij}), where B = DC = (b_{ij}) is the symmetrized Cartan matrix, so b_{ii} = 2d_i and b_{ij} = d_i c_{ij} < 0 for i ∼ j. Diagram (2.2) displays the oriented cycle used to define the potential S; it shows a vertex (i, m - b_{ii}) with an arrow to (i,m) and an arrow to (j, m + b_{ij}).
candidates.suspected_defect: The arrow from (i, m - b_{ii}) to (j, m + b_{ij}) contradicts the defining rule: an arrow out of (i, m-b_{ii}) must land on (j, m - b_{ii} + b_{ij}), not (j, m + b_{ij}). The arrow into (j, m + b_{ij}) should emanate from (i,m). As drawn, the displayed cycle is not a cycle in Γ, so the potential is defined from an incorrect diagram.

candidates.claim_content: Here r is the lacing number of g, d_i are the symmetrizer entries with B = DC symmetric, ε_i are the loops at vertex i in the quiver Q̃ with deg(ε_i) = (b_{ii},0) = (2d_i,0), and Π̃ is the generalized preprojective algebra. The element ε is defined as Σ_{i∈I} ε_i^{r/d} e_i and Π(l) := Π̃ / ε^l Π̃.
candidates.suspected_defect: The exponent r/d uses an undefined symbol 'd' (presumably d_i, i.e. ε = Σ_i ε_i^{r/d_i} e_i, which is what makes ε homogeneous and central); with a global d the element ε is not homogeneous in general. Also ε^l Π̃ is only a right ideal; the quotient algebra requires the two-sided ideal Π̃ ε^l Π̃ (ε is central only if the exponents are r/d_i). This definition is used in Proposition 2.1.
